links.comparator_used: Independent clinician re-review of a random sample of 100 triage-rated 'good' conversations, used as the reference standard. Flagged conversations also went to expert review.
links.outcome: Triage sensitivity for clinically critical events, and reduction in the number of conversations needing expert review
links.effect: Triage flagged 212/2035 conversations (10.4%). 45 went to specialist adjudication and 5 were confirmed critical, with 40 judged non-critical. In the random sample of 100 'good'-rated conversations, 4 (4%; 95% CI 1.6-9.8) had clinically critical errors the triage missed. Rated good: 1803/2035 (88.6%).
links.tradeoff: A conditional false-negative rate of about 4% within the 'good' stratum, from a single window and a small sample with a wide CI. 40 of the 45 conversations escalated for specialist review were false positives. The triage model had no prior disease-specific validation. The triage ran as one post-hoc batch, not in real time.
links.quote: Of 100 conversations randomly drawn from the AI-classified “good” stratum (1803 conversations), 4 contained critical safety issues after independent clinical review and adjudication (4%; 95% CI 1·6–9·8).

design_hint: conversation-level post-market surveillance with expert review
